one_sentence: This paper argues that the theophysical method, which restores 'Why' to inquiry, survives scientific scrutiny and outperforms naturalism in explanatory power across foundational phenomena.
executive_summary: This document presents a comprehensive defense of the theophysical method, a framework that integrates theology and science by restoring the question 'Why' to the center of inquiry. It argues that the current replication crisis in science (with replication rates as low as 11% in some fields) stems from a methodological ban on causal explanation. The paper introduces new metrics—the Universal Theory Defense Grading System (UTDGS) and 12 Structural Coherence Invariants—to evaluate theories beyond citation counts and peer review. It presents bidirectional evidence: 12 biblical claims confirmed by science with an average 2,700-year priority gap, and 10 empirical results that naturalism cannot explain without unfalsifiable speculation. A comparative scorecard gives biblical theism 39/50 versus naturalism's 21/50 across foundational phenomena. The paper concludes that while both systems are circular in their axioms, the theophysical framework achieves cross-domain synthesis across 45 domains and has a live falsification test scheduled for October 2026. The authors acknowledge weaknesses, including the problem of suffering and self-scoring biases, and invite external falsification.
short_summary: This document is a formal paper defending the theophysical method as a testable, falsifiable framework for cross-domain synthesis. Its core structural claim is that restoring 'Why' to inquiry resolves fragmentation and outperforms naturalism in explanatory power. Key evidence includes 12 biblical claims confirmed by science with a 2,700-year average priority gap and 10 empirical results naturalism cannot explain. This matters because it offers a unified framework that passes scientific scrutiny while addressing foundational questions, with a live falsification test scheduled for October 2026.
